NONE: B1 also 'd used to refer to future time from the point of view of the past
（從過去的角度指將來發生的事）將，將要
› used to refer back to a time in the past from a point of view in the future
（從將來的角度指過去應該發生的事）就會，應該
› also 'd used to refer to an intention from the point of view of the past
（從過去的角度指某一意圖）將，會，要
B1 also 'd used to refer to a situation that you can imagine happening
（指想像會發生的情形）會，將
B1 also 'd used with if in conditional sentences (= sentences that refer to what happens if something else happens)
（與 if 引導的條件句連用）
A1 also 'd used in polite requests and offers
（用於提要求時代替 will，語氣更加客氣）
B1 past simple of
will modal verb(ABLE/WILLING) : used to talk about what someone was willing to do or what something was able to do
B1 used to show that you prefer to have or do one thing more than another
更願意；情願
› used to express a strong wish or desire
要是…多好；但願
B2 also 'd used to talk about things in the past that happened often or always
（用於談論過去經常或總是發生的事）常常，總是
› also 'd disapproving used to suggest that what happens is expected because it is typical, especially of a person's behaviour
（用於指某人的典型行為）老是，總是
C1 also 'd used to express an opinion in a polite way without being forceful
（用於禮貌地表明觀點）
› also 'd used after "I" when giving advice
（表示勸告）
› also 'd used after "why" when giving or asking the reason for something
（給出或詢問原因時用於why之後）竟會
› also 'd used to refer to what is very likely
可能；大概

example: He said he would see his brother tomorrow.
他說明天要去見他的兄弟。
They knew there would be trouble unless the report was finished by the next day.
他們知道，除非第二天能完成報告，否則就有麻煩了。
We realized it wouldn't be easy to find another secretary.
我們意識到再找一位秘書不會很容易。
We thought they would have got home by five o'clock, but there was no reply when we phoned.
我們以為他們會在五時前到家，可是打電話時卻沒有人接聽。
They promised that they would help.
他們承諾會幫忙。
There was nobody left who would (= was willing to) do it.
剩下的人裡沒人願意做這件事。
I asked him to move his car but he said he wouldn't (= he refused).
我要他挪一下車，可是他拒絕了。
I would hate to miss the show.
錯過這次演出，我會很遺憾的。
I'd go myself but I'm too busy.
我要不是太忙，就會親自去。
It would have been very boring to sit through the whole speech.
若當時聽完整場演講的話，會是十分枯燥的。
What would you do if you lost your job?
要是失去了工作，你會怎麼辦？
If I'd had time, I would have gone to see Graham.
如果那時我有時間的話，我本來會去看望格拉漢姆的。

NONE: C2 If you would (just) as soon do something or would sooner do something, you would prefer to do it rather than something else that is possible.
寧可，寧願

example: "Would you like to go out for dinner?" "I'd just as soon stay in - I'm not feeling very well."
「出去吃飯怎麽樣？」「我寧願待在家裡——我有些不舒服。」

NONE: › used to say that nothing could persuade you to do something
絕對不做，無論如何都不做

example: I wouldn't take that job for all the tea in China.
我決不會去做那個工作。

NONE: A1 used when offering something or inviting someone
你想（做）…嗎？你是否願意…？

example: Would you like a drink?
你想喝點甚麽嗎？
Would you like to join us for dinner tonight?
你願意今晚和我們一起共進晚餐嗎？
Would you like me to take you in the car?
我開車送你好嗎？

NONE: C2 wanting or trying to be
想要做…的；試圖成為…的；未來的

example: a would-be artist/politician
未來的藝術家／政治家

NONE: › short form of would not
（would not 的縮略形式）

example: I wouldn't do that if I were you.
我要是你的話，就不會那樣做。

NONE: › If someone wouldn't be seen dead in a particular place or doing a particular thing, they would never do it, usually because it would be too embarrassing.
（通常因爲會太尷尬而）絕不會做

example: I wouldn't be seen dead wearing a dress like that.
我才不會穿那樣的裙子呢。

NONE: C2 used to say that you would not do something because you think it is wrong or silly
根本不會去做，絕不會去做

example: My father is very generous, but I wouldn't dream of actually asking him for money!
我父親很慷慨，但我絕不會去向他要錢！

NONE: › used to say that you would not want a situation to be different, even though it has problems connected with it
（即使遇到困難也）不後悔

example: It's never going to be easy having kids but I wouldn't have it any other way.
養孩子不容易，但我毫無怨言。

NONE: › If you say that someone wouldn't hurt a fly, you mean they are gentle and would not do anything to injure or offend anyone.
連一隻蒼蠅都不肯傷害，心地善良
› used to say that someone would not recognize something even if it was obvious

NONE: › used to mean that you certainly do not want to buy something or be involved with something
壓根不想買；根本不想與…有瓜葛
